newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: WMC eyes further copper output increase.
newsitem.headline: WMC eyes further copper output increase.

text.p: WMC Ltd said on Monday it is seeking environmental approvals to further increase annual production of copper and other metals at its Olympic Dam project in South Australia in the next century to 350,000 tonnes.
Current annual production from Olympic Dam is 85,000 tonnes of copper a year, although WMC said it holds government environmental approvals to lift yearly output to up to 150,000 tonnes in 1999.

WMC said an environmental impact statement released on Monday seeks federal and state approvals to lift annual output by another 50,000 tonnes by the end of 1999 and further increase production to 350,000 tonnes at a later date.

At an annual rate of 200,000 tonnes, the value production of copper and associated products at Olympic Dam would total about A$650 million, rising to A$1.11 billion at 350,000 tonnes, based on December 1996 metals prices, WMC said.
This compares with annual sales in 1995/96 (July-June) of almost A$390 million WMC said.

WMC said it has no present plans to increase output above 200,000 tonnes, although environmental approval would provide flexibility to plan production over the long term, taking into account metals prices, operating costs and changes in processing technology.

"To model the longer term impacts of Olympic Dam on the state and national economics and water supplies in the Great Artesian Basin, it has been assumed in the EIS that construction of a second phase expansion increasing production to 350,000 tonnes per annum of copper would begin in the year 2008 and that the cost of this phase would be an additional A$900 million over
a two year period," it said.
The cost of the current expansion has been estimated by WMC at A$1.48 billion.

WMC managing director Hugh Morgan earlier this year said Olympic Dam's uranium output at the end of 1999 would be over 3,700 tonnes and gold production would be roughly 75,000 ounces, while silver production would hit one million ounces.
